case_name: Orissa Judicial Services Association Cuttack and Another v State of Orissa and Others
petitioner: Orissa Judicial Services Association Cuttack and Another
facts: The Orissa Judicial Services Association has filed this petition under Article 32 of the Constitution challenging the constitutional validity of Rule 7 of the Orissa Superior Judicial Service Rules, 1963 and for quashing Notification dated February 24, 1987 inviting applications from members of the bar for direct recruitment to the Orissa Superior Judicial Service.

The petitioner-Association, which represents the members of the Judicial Service of the State of Orissa has raised grievance that the Sub-ordinate Judicial Service in the State continues to be in a pitiable condition and most of the judicial officers have been stagnating for many years for lack of promotional avenues.

Their grievance is that there should be no direct recruitment to the Superior Judicial Service and in that view they have challenged the Notification dated February 24, 1987 issued by the High Court inviting applications from the members of the bar for direct recruitment to the Superior Judicial Service.
issues: The constitutional validity of Rule 7 of the Orissa Superior Judicial Service Rules, 1963
Whether the State Government and the High Court are acting contrary to law in making direct recruitments to the Superior Judicial Service
petitioner_arguments: The petitioner's grievance that direct recruitment of the members of the bar is not permissible under the law and that the State Government and the High Court are acting contrary to law in making direct recruitments to the Superior Judicial Service is devoid of any merit.
There should be no direct recruitment to the Superior Judicial Service
respondent_arguments: The State Government as well as the High Court both have filed counter-affidavits contesting the petition

The Governor of Orissa has in consultation with the High Court, in exercise of powers under Article 309 read with Article 233 of the Constitution, framed the Orissa Superior Judicial Service Rules, 1963 regulating the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to the Orissa Superior Judicial Service.
court_reasoning: The constitutional mandate cannot be challenge merely because it may to certain extent adversely affect the chances of promotion of the Junior Branch of Judicial Service.

There is further no dispute between the parties that the quota of 25 per cent and 75 per cent for direct recruitment and promotees has been followed and in actual practice the State Government in consultation with the High Court has ensured that the quota of 75 per cent fixed for promotees has been maintained.
holding: The petition is accordingly dismissed, but there will be no order as to costs.
cases_cited: Orissa Judicial Services Association Cuttack and Another v State of Orissa
